scope: Browser walkthrough of every menu destination, from the perspective of a tired patient or carer. A design/engineering audit, not a patient study or clinical review.
environment: Codex in-app Chromium browser; desktop entry and 390 × 844 phone viewport; 100% and 200% app text. Forms used a separate localhost:4175 origin with invented notes. Existing personal saved data on localhost:4173 was not opened, changed or deleted.
verdict: The home and card choices are useful. The inner experience still demands too much reading and remembering. Three confirmed functional failures need repair before describing the experience as suitable for low vision or memory difficulties.
limits: No NVDA, VoiceOver, TalkBack, physical-phone touch, manual browser zoom, clinical accuracy, external-site validation or patient/carer session was performed. The scroll failure was reproduced with browser pointer scrolling. Card preview was exercised; downloads and printing were outside this audit. No app source was changed.
strengths: Four clear home actions, readable text and calm rounded surfaces.
A communication statement created a useful card preview without a name or medical details.
The practical card draft remained available in app memory; the saved hub labelled it as unsaved.
Fatigue search returned the intended guide, without putting the query in the address.
Urgent help remained easy to find and led to direct generic instructions.
Escape closed the menu and returned focus to Menu. Keyboard Enter on the skip link focused the active main region.

findings.title: Enlarged menu cannot reach its bottom
findings.evidence: At 390 × 844 and 200% app text, Saved occupied y=827–936 and About y=940–995. Pointer scrolling over the menu left scrollTop at zero. The main region collapsed to zero height while the expanded menu was outside its scroll area.
findings.patientEffect: Someone needing large text cannot reach the saved-items and privacy menu entries using ordinary scrolling.
findings.fix: Give the menu a bounded, independently scrollable region while keeping Close menu and urgent help reachable. Test the open menu at small heights and large text, not just individual routes.

findings.title: Appointment and support drafts disappear on return
findings.evidence: An invented appointment note was entered, then Home → Prepare an appointment returned an empty note with no warning. A support note and checked statement also disappeared after Home → Menu → Support preferences. These were unsaved drafts; saved records were not deleted.
findings.patientEffect: The person must reconstruct their wording and selections, and may not remember what was lost. The card tool behaves differently because it preserves drafts.
findings.fix: Retain both sheet drafts in app-session memory, as cards do. Keep persistent Save explicit; do not introduce silent storage. Show saved/unsaved status near the working controls.

findings.title: Simplified reading can strand the reader on one section
findings.evidence: Global Simplified reading was enabled. On the recovery guide, turning off Read one section at a time unchecked the control and removed Next/Previous. Only the first of five sections remained; the other section headings were absent.
findings.patientEffect: The control appears off, but the remaining information cannot be reached from that view.
findings.fix: Use one effective reading-mode state for the checkbox, visible sections and pagination. Either support a local override or clearly present the global setting as authoritative.

findings.title: Useful content is buried below setup and repeated notices
findings.evidence: The guide library, recovery guide and glossary showed no guide body/definition in the first phone viewport. The recovery page places save/print/read-aloud controls and three reading/action panels before its first section.
findings.patientEffect: Opening a topic feels like another setup task. Tired readers must scroll before receiving the help they came for.
findings.fix: Keep a short visible draft label, then show useful content or one immediate action. Move detailed review/privacy explanations and secondary tools into labelled disclosures. Retain review dates, source limits and personal-care boundaries.

findings.title: Returning to reading still requires remembering
findings.evidence: After saving the recovery guide and reaching section 2, returning through Home → Saved → Saved guides → recovery reset the one-section mode and reading position. The library search also reset on return.
findings.patientEffect: Bookmarks help find the topic but do not help the person continue where they stopped.
findings.fix: Preserve reading mode/section and search state in app-session memory. Offer a generic Continue reading entry without exposing health details on Home. Discuss explicit local persistence separately.

findings.title: The carer entry gives a reading list before a practical action
findings.evidence: Help someone starts with a draft notice and six guide links. The support-sheet and appointment actions come after that list.
findings.patientEffect: A worried family member has to make another reading choice before doing something useful.
findings.fix: Lead with a few small actions: ask what help is wanted, prepare one question, or review support preferences together. Keep optional reading underneath.

findings.title: Guide text-size radios do not expose checked state
findings.evidence: The rendered Standard text/Larger text radios had aria-selected true/false, but aria-checked was absent on both. This was a DOM check, not an NVDA test.
findings.patientEffect: Assistive technology may not communicate the current choice correctly. The page-local controls also duplicate Text and display.
findings.fix: Use proper radio checked state and keyboard behavior, or consolidate these controls into the global display preferences.

findings.title: MRI search leads to an unhelpful dead end
findings.evidence: Searching the glossary for MRI returned zero terms, a try-a-shorter-word message and a clinician prompt. There was no route to the tests/scans guide from that empty state.
findings.patientEffect: The app promises help with report words but cannot give a useful next destination for this query.
findings.fix: Link the empty state to Tests, scans and unfamiliar terms. Expand terms and synonyms only with the required content review.

findings.title: Resource trust labels are confusing and overly technical
findings.evidence: The directory says 5 verified resources while every item shows Source appraisal: candidate and Clinical review: not recorded. Rights annotations and internal source-type names are displayed on each item.
findings.patientEffect: The reader cannot tell whether verified means the link was checked or the clinical content was approved.
findings.fix: Say Links checked when that is the evidence. Present audience, publisher, link date and relevant limits plainly; retain detailed rights/appraisal records behind Source details.

findings.title: The no-typing communication path is hidden after typing fields
findings.evidence: The practical card starts with name and a large free-text box. Choose communication statements sits below them and is collapsed.
findings.patientEffect: Someone with communication or typing difficulty can miss the easiest way to create a useful card.
findings.fix: Offer the selectable statements first, with optional own words and personal details underneath. Keep the two card models separate.

steps.title: Current desktop guide library
steps.note: Readable and consistent, but a large introduction and draft notice precede the guide list.

steps.title: Guide library on a phone
steps.note: No guide is visible in the first viewport; the introduction and search explanation take the space.

steps.title: Return Home
steps.note: Four understandable actions fit the ordinary phone view. This is the strongest navigation improvement.

steps.title: Open the full menu
steps.note: All nine items fit at standard text, but the menu displaces most of the page. Some labels overlap in purpose.

steps.title: Search for fatigue
steps.note: One relevant result appears. Reaching the search still requires scrolling past preliminaries.

steps.title: Open recovery guidance
steps.note: The first viewport ends near Save; the guide body is below multiple setup panels.

steps.title: Choose one section at a time
steps.note: The counter and Next control are clear. There are still many controls before the content; radio checked state is missing.

steps.title: Start appointment questions
steps.note: Five suggested questions are preselected, but the first view mainly asks the person to configure their reading pace.

steps.title: Write an invented appointment note
steps.note: The field is labelled; preview and Save are farther down. No personal data was used.

steps.title: Return to the appointment sheet
steps.note: The invented note is gone after Home and return. There was no navigation warning.

steps.title: Choose a card
steps.note: Two separate, understandable purposes; neither requires identifying information.

steps.title: Open the practical card form
steps.note: Short optional form, but the easier statement selection sits below the typing area.

steps.title: Preview a communication statement
steps.note: A useful card can be prepared without a name or health details. The safety label is visible.

steps.title: Open the milestone form
steps.note: Neutral title, optional name/message, optional date and survivor wording. Export was not exercised in this audit.

steps.title: Try Help someone
steps.note: A family member gets another guide catalogue before the practical tools.

steps.title: Open support preferences
steps.note: The statements are useful, but introductory panels and pace controls precede them.

steps.title: Choose a statement and write an invented support note
steps.note: The note and selection are visible; persistence still requires the separate Save action.

steps.title: Return to support preferences
steps.note: Both the invented note and the selected statement are lost.

steps.title: Look up a term
steps.note: The purpose is clear, but search is below repeated explanatory panels.

steps.title: Search MRI
steps.note: Zero results, with no link to the existing tests/scans guide.

steps.title: Open Resources
steps.note: Useful external destinations, but verified/candidate labels and rights text make the directory harder to interpret.

steps.title: Find saved items and card drafts
steps.note: Generic labels protect details. The practical card draft is still available, unlike the two sheet drafts.

steps.title: Read About and privacy
steps.note: Honest boundaries and deletion access, but a long project explanation precedes the practical privacy controls.

steps.title: Find Text and display
steps.note: Plain labels, usable controls and a persistent header entry. This was tested only on the separate audit origin.

steps.title: Open Menu at 200% app text
steps.note: Saved and About fall below the viewport; the main region has zero height.

steps.title: Try to scroll the enlarged menu
steps.note: Pointer scrolling does not reveal the bottom entries. Escape still closes the menu and returns focus.

steps.title: Open Urgent help
steps.note: Direct generic emergency wording, without scoring, automatic calls or graphic imagery. Clinical wording was not assessed.

steps.title: Read section 2 of a saved guide
steps.note: The section counter and Next/Previous work within the current view.

steps.title: Return through the saved guide list
steps.note: The topic is saved. This requires an extra list screen and repeats the draft notice.

steps.title: Reopen the saved guide
steps.note: One-section mode and reading position reset. Saving a topic is not a resume-reading function.

steps.title: Enable global Simplified reading
steps.note: The guide opens in one-section mode; the introductory panels remain unchanged.

steps.title: Turn off the guide's one-section toggle
steps.note: The checkbox becomes unchecked and the paging controls disappear, but global Simplified reading still restricts the content to one section.
